e: The US begins direct negotiations with the military junta while continuing sanctions against its leader, Min Aung Hlaing, for human rights violations, notably the Rohingya genocide.
Malaysia begins the repatriation of 5,000 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.
Fifty people are killed in a Tatmadaw airstrike on Kyauktaw, Rakhine State.
A fighter aircraft of the Myanmar Air Force crashes in Hmawbi Township following a birdstrike. The pilot ejects safely.
An agreement is reached for Myanmar to accept back around 5,000 Rohingya refugees residing in Malaysia.
A former president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Myanmar is arrested in Yangon as part of an investigation into alleged suspicious financial transactions by former members of the board.
Min Aung Hlaing arrives in India for a five-day state visit.
The Thai–Myanmar Friendship Bridge No.2 is opened for the first time in more than 10 months.
The Myanmar-Thai border town of Mawdaung, Tanintharyi Region is captured by the Tatmadaw from the KNU/KNLA.
A US diplomat is found fatally stabbed at a hotel in Yangon.
A truck overturns in Ottarathiri Township, Naypyidaw Union Territory, killing 16 people and injuring 21 others.
Aung San Suu Kyi has her prison sentence shortened by one-sixth and commuted to house arrest for her remaining sentence.
A bus collides with a van in Thaton Township, Mon State, killing 13 people.

Min Aung Hlaing issues an amnesty for 4,335 prisoners and commutes all active death sentences to life imprisonment. The amnesty also sees the release of former president Win Myint and a reduction in the prison sentence for opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi.
Min Aung Hlaing is officially sworn in as president of Myanmar, along with his cabinet.
The KNU ratifies the interim Kawtholei Charter and establishes Kawtholei Consultative Council and Kawtholei Governing Council.
The Presidential Electoral College opens nominations for the 2026 Myanmar presidential election being held in April
General Ye Win Oo succeeds Senior-General Min Aung Hlaing as Commander-in-Chief of Defence Services.

The Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw, National Unity Government, the Kachin Independence Organisation, the Karen National Union, the Karenni State Interim Executive Council, and the Chin National Front form a Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union (SCEF).
The Third Amyotha Hluttaw is convened at Nay Pyi Taw. Aung Lin Dwe is elected as Speaker.
The Third Pyithu Hluttaw is convened at Naypyidaw. USDP party leader Khin Yi is elected as Speaker.
The Tatmadaw retakes Tagaung, the last NUG-held town in Mandalay Region.
The United Kingdom suspends the issuance of student visas to Burmese nationals as part of efforts to reduce asylum requests.
The junta issues an amnesty for more than 7,300 prisoners convicted on terrorism-related charges.
At least 25 people are killed in a Tatmadaw airstrike on a trading post in the village of Pyaung in Mindon Township, Magway Region.
At least 17 people are killed in a Tatmadaw airstrike on the village of Yoengu in Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine State.
Bo Nagar, a leader of the Burma National Revolutionary Army (BNRA), surrenders to the Tatmadaw in Sagaing Region.
Myanmar expels East Timorese charge d’affaires Elisio do Rosario de Sousa in response to investigations in Timor-Leste against the junta for war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Myanmar and Russia sign a five-year military cooperation agreement.
A magnitude 6.0 earthquake hits Rakhine State.
China executes four members of the Bai crime family that ran scam centres in Laukkai.
China executes 11 members of the Ming crime family that ran scam centres in Laukkai.
At least 21 people are killed in a Tatmadaw airstrike on the village of Hteelin in Bhamo Township, Kachin State.
The junta issues pardons for 6,134 prisoners to mark 78 years of independence from the United Kingdom.
